title: The Disappearance of Flight MH370, Part II
summary: Part two of a two-part episode on the disappearance of Malaysia Airlines Flight MH370 in March 2014. The hosts pick up after the crash, covering the bungled post-crash investigation under Malaysia's government, the failed multinational searches in the South China Sea and Southern Indian Ocean, the private search by Ocean Infinity, the Independent Group of online enthusiasts, debris found on Reunion Island and along the African coast (including the flaperon and Blaine Gibson's finds), and the physics of the plane breaking up on impact. They discuss evidence pointing to Captain Zaharie Ahmad Shah deliberately crashing the plane, his simulator flight, and the personal circumstances reported about him, then run through conspiracy theories (cyber hijacking, Bermuda Triangle, MH17 false flag, FreeScale Semiconductor employees, alien abduction). The episode opens with a sponsor-style appeal for Australian wildfire relief and closes with listener mail about a Michigan family's cardiac arrest and CPR.

segments.title: Opening banter, tour dates, and Australia wildfire relief
segments.summary: The hosts plug upcoming San Francisco SketchFest performances and a live show, then read listener mail from Sally M. in Sydney about the Australian wildfires and list charities to donate to, including Australian Red Cross, Salvation Army Australia, WIRES, the Port Macquarie Koala Hospital, and the NSW Rural Fire Service families fund.

segments.title: Introduction and bungled Malaysian investigation
segments.summary: The hosts introduce part two of MH370 and recap that the investigation was bungled, attributing it to Malaysia's government-controlled airline and the political climate. They note the government bought back Malaysian Airlines shares after MH17 was shot down in 2014.

segments.title: Early search efforts and the Joint Investigation Team
segments.summary: The hosts describe the initial search in the South China Sea, the Australian-led coordination center, the delayed move to the Southern Indian Ocean, and the Malaysian-led Joint Investigation Team with the US, China, Britain and France. They criticize Malaysia's preliminary and final reports and air traffic control failures, and note the military's delayed disclosure.

segments.title: Passenger checks, final search results, and Ocean Infinity
segments.summary: The hosts discuss police background checks finding two Iranian passengers with stolen passports, the final report's praise of Captain Zaharie, the two-year search costing around $160 million, and the official conclusion that the plane ended in the Southern Indian Ocean. They then describe the private Ocean Infinity search and its autonomous underwater vehicles.

segments.title: The Independent Group and raw satellite data
segments.summary: The hosts describe the Independent Group of online enthusiasts, including engineers and specialists, who helped analyze the data and were acknowledged by the Australian government. They say the group obtained raw Inmarsat data through a family member when it was not released officially.

segments.title: Debris found on Reunion Island and the breakup on impact
segments.summary: The hosts discuss Blaine Gibson's search for wreckage along African coasts and the 2015 discovery of a flaperon on Reunion Island, which confirmed the plane crashed in the Indian Ocean. They explain that the plane likely broke apart on impact, which would explain why the emergency beacons failed and why the black boxes may not be recoverable.

segments.title: Captain Zaharie and the pilot-suicide theory
segments.summary: The hosts argue no one claimed responsibility, making terrorism unlikely, and examine evidence pointing to Captain Zaharie Ahmad Shah: his separation from his wife, a relationship with a married woman, and a flight simulator flight that matched the final path. They describe how he could have locked out the first officer and说 the plane was flown deliberately into the ocean, comparing it to other pilot murder-suicides such as Germanwings, EgyptAir 990, and SilkAir 185, while stressing that it cannot be proven.

segments.title: MH370 conspiracy theories
segments.summary: The hosts run through popular conspiracy theories: cyber hijacking of the autopilot, a link to MH17 as a false flag, the Bermuda Triangle, the FreeScale Semiconductor employees on board, and alien abduction, which they dismiss or find implausible.

segments.title: Listener mail: CPR save from Tyler Elliott
segments.summary: Tyler Elliott from Michigan writes that his wife suffered cardiac arrest the Sunday before Thanksgiving; he used CPR advice from the show, including the rhythm of 'Stayin' Alive,' and EMTs used a defibrillator and epinephrine. She has brain damage but a good recovery chance. He thanks the hosts and his friend Justin.

segments.title: Outro
segments.summary: The hosts thank listeners, point to the website and social links, and give the contact email and iHeartRadio podcast information.
